correctness.rationale: The diagram orders and arm lengths agree with the claimed finite simple graphs. Four ordered choices with replacement and a terminal diagram distinguishing equality, adjacency and neither give a complete EF invariant by backwards induction using sets of next-choice types. An independently written enumeration reproduces the entire finite partition through parameter 40 for A,D and includes E6, E7 and E8. The virtual-endpoint strategy handles the infinite tails: a gap count measures unused interior vertices, the thresholds are 1,3,7,15,31, and a gap above threshold can absorb a move while matching a short side exactly or leaving enough on both sides. Equality and adjacency are preserved at threshold 1; a move at an already paired endpoint or extra pendant preserves the invariant at the lower threshold. In D_n the spine has n−4 interior vertices and the two off-spine vertices meet only the paired trivalent end. Thus A≥33 and D≥35 each stabilize, and the exhaustive finite checks bridge those tails to A16 and D17, including all cross-series distinctions. The D17 class has no smaller representative inside the listed family, so the sharp ceiling is 17, not a claim about all finite graphs.
residual_risks: The finite run establishes the bridge and distinctions within the enumerated range; the unbounded conclusion uses the separately checked gap lemma. No claim for richer diagram signatures or other families.

The exact trivalent-family stabilization and comparisons tell when distinct orders are no longer discernible and whether exceptional diagram types can be confused with other diagrams.
